collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: Out alone past the reef, a villager feels whales singing through the wood of the canoe and lies down to listen.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: (name1) is out in the canoe alone, well past the reef, on a calm grey morning with the line slack in the water. Then (he/she) feels it before (he/she) hears it: a low hum coming up through the wood of the canoe, through (his/her) knees, through (his/her) chest. Then a long, rising call, and another, and another, sliding up and down like someone singing very slowly in a voice as big as the sea. Somewhere below, out of sight, whales are singing. (name1) pulls in the line and lies down in the bottom of the canoe with (his/her) ear against the wood and listens. (He/she) has no idea what they're saying. (He/she) is fairly sure it isn't about (him/her). It goes on for a long time, and then it stops, and the sea is just the sea again. (name1) paddles home without a single fish and doesn't care at all.
